import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 845

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/845](https://www.erdosproblems.com/845)
-/

namespace Erdos845

/--
Let $C > 0$. Is it true that the set of integers of the form $n = b_1 + \cdots + b_t$,
with $b_1 < \cdots < b_t$, where $b_i = 2^{k_i}3^{l_i}$ for $1 \leq i\leq t$ and
$b_t \leq Cb_1$ has density $0$?

van Doorn and Everts \cite{vDEv25} have disproved this with $C=6$ - in fact, they prove that all
integers can be written as such a sum in which $b_t<6b_1$.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos845.lean"]
theorem erdos_845 :
    answer(False) ↔
      ∀ᵉ (C : ℝ) (hC : 0 < C),
        let f : ℕ × ℕ → ℕ := fun (k, l) ↦ 2 ^ k * 3 ^ l
        { ∑ x ∈ B, f x | (B : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) (h : B.Nonempty)
          (hB : B.sup f ≤ C * B.inf' h f) }.HasDensity 0 := by
  sorry

end Erdos845

reformulations.difference: The source uses an increasing sequence of distinct 3-smooth summands. Lean instead sums over a nonempty finite set of exponent pairs, using Finset.sup and Finset.inf' for the largest and smallest summands.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The map (k,l) ↦ 2^k * 3^l is positive and injective by unique prime factorization. Consequently, sorting the image of a nonempty exponent-pair finset gives exactly an increasing sequence of distinct allowed summands, preserving its sum and extrema. Conversely, choosing the exponent pair for each term of such a sequence gives a valid finset with the same sum and bound. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, proved representability equivalence for every C > 0 and n, then lifted it to equivalence of the universally quantified density questions. The proofs depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

review.notes: No mathematical defects found. The source records DISPROVED (LEAN), consistent with research solved and answer(False). The paper proves that every positive integer has a representation with largest summand < 6 times the smallest, refuting the globally quantified density-zero question. Lean tests verified that zero is never represented, C < 1 gives the empty set, and C = 1 gives exactly the 3-smooth integers; computations also checked representations through 20. Density uses finite initial-segment counts, so ncard's infinite-set default is unreachable. Direct website access was challenged, and its text-reader copy omitted equations; the mathematical conventions were checked against the paper's LaTeX. The linked formal proof matches the declaration and contains no explicit proof holes or custom axioms. Its pinned Lean 4.24.0 build was not reproduced: compiling it under the sandbox's Lean 4.33.1 produced version/API incompatibilities, not evidence of a status defect.
